_comment: Batch 06 (Sets 10-11). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason. PN-S10-06 (single-word drainage terms) is in skipped.json.

RN-S10-02.A: Document the normal oxygen saturation of 99% and continue routine monitoring
RN-S10-02.C: Apply oxygen at 2 L/min by nasal cannula and recheck the oxygen saturation in 1 hour
RN-S10-02.D: Encourage deep breathing and coughing, then reassess the client in 1 hour

RN-S10-05.A: Edema of the burned arm that has gradually increased since the client's admission
RN-S10-05.C: Pain at the edges of the burn, where the skin is partial thickness
RN-S10-05.D: Dry, leathery, waxy white appearance of the burned skin on the upper arm

RN-S10-07.B: Allergy to shellfish such as shrimp

RN-S10-08.A: Low-calorie, low-protein diet to reduce the workload on the kidneys
RN-S10-08.C: Clear liquids only for the first 2 weeks after the burn injury
RN-S10-08.D: Low-fat, low-sodium diet only, with calories kept at the client's usual level

RN-S10-09.A: Dress the small entry and exit wounds with sterile gauze
RN-S10-09.C: Calculate the TBSA burned using the rule of nines
RN-S10-09.D: Apply cool compresses to the entry and exit wounds

RN-S10-10.A: Immediately flush the arms with large amounts of running water
RN-S10-10.C: Apply a weak acid such as vinegar to neutralize the lime
RN-S10-10.D: Cover the arms with dry, sterile dressings and transfer the client

RN-S10-14.A: Restart the device over the existing foam dressing and resume the prescribed settings
RN-S10-14.C: Leave the foam dressing in place until the next scheduled dressing change in 2 days
RN-S10-14.D: Increase the suction pressure when restarting to make up for the time it was off

RN-S10-15.A: Apply a tight compression bandage from the toes up to the knee each morning
RN-S10-15.C: Keep the leg in a dependent position to improve blood flow to the area
RN-S10-15.D: Massage the reddened area gently to reduce the swelling in the leg

RN-S10-16.A: Simple cellulitis that will respond to oral antibiotics
RN-S10-16.C: Contact dermatitis from a reaction to the wound dressing
RN-S10-16.D: Normal wound healing with expected inflammation around the edges

RN-S10-17.A: Continuing the medication and adding an oral antihistamine for the rash
RN-S10-17.C: Applying hydrocortisone cream to the rash and discharging the client home today
RN-S10-17.D: Doubling the dose to gain better control of the client's seizures

RN-S10-18.A: "It's fine if I get pregnant while taking this, as long as I stop the medicine as soon as I find out."
RN-S10-18.C: "I'll take extra vitamin A supplements every day to help my skin clear up faster."
RN-S10-18.D: "I can still donate blood at the community blood drive at work while I'm taking this."

RN-S10-24.A: Apply topical antimicrobial cream to all of the burned areas
RN-S10-24.C: Administer the prescribed tetanus toxoid injection IM
RN-S10-24.D: Obtain photographs of the burns for the medical record

RN-S11-06.A: Continue the infusion, since the sodium level is still below the normal range
RN-S11-06.C: Increase the infusion rate to reach a normal sodium level sooner
RN-S11-06.D: Encourage the client to drink more water with meals and snacks

RN-S11-07.A: Weight gain, bounding pulses, and distended jugular veins
RN-S11-07.C: Muscle cramps, weakness, and U waves on the ECG
RN-S11-07.D: Positive Trousseau's sign and numbness around the mouth

RN-S11-09.A: Tetany, carpopedal spasm, and seizure activity
RN-S11-09.C: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes and muscle twitching
RN-S11-09.D: Diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and a positive Chvostek's sign

RN-S11-11.A: Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes with muscle twitching and tremors
RN-S11-11.C: Tetany with carpopedal spasm and painful muscle cramps
RN-S11-11.D: Tachycardia and hypertension with a pounding headache

PN-S10-02.A: Grasp the client under both arms and pull the client up toward the headboard
PN-S10-02.C: Have the client bend both knees and push up in bed with the heels on the mattress
PN-S10-02.D: Raise the head of the bed to 60 degrees before moving the client up

PN-S10-03.B: A shallow open wound with a pink, moist wound bed and no slough
PN-S10-03.C: A deep, crater-like wound with bone visible at the base
PN-S10-03.D: An intact, fluid-filled blister over the back of the heel

PN-S10-04.A: Place a soft pillow directly under both heels to cushion them
PN-S10-04.C: Massage the heels firmly every shift to improve circulation
PN-S10-04.D: Keep the heels resting directly on the mattress with a sheet over them

PN-S10-05.A: Wash the area with a harsh deodorant soap and scrub the skin well to remove all of the urine
PN-S10-05.C: Leave the client in the wet brief until the next scheduled check in 2 hours
PN-S10-05.D: Apply a thick layer of powder to the perineal area after each episode

PN-S10-07.A: Clean from the outer skin toward the incision in a circular motion
PN-S10-07.C: Use the same gauze pad to clean the entire length of the incision
PN-S10-07.D: Scrub back and forth across the incision with a moistened gauze pad

PN-S10-08.A: Leave the bulb fully expanded so that the drainage can flow freely
PN-S10-08.C: Irrigate the drain with sterile saline to keep it patent
PN-S10-08.D: Remove the drain once it has been emptied and measured

PN-S10-09.B: Black, dry, hard, and leathery tissue
PN-S10-09.C: Yellow, stringy tissue that is loose and moist
PN-S10-09.D: Pale, dry tissue with little or no bleeding

PN-S10-10.A: "Put ice directly on it right away to stop the pain."
PN-S10-10.C: "Apply butter or cooking oil to soothe the burn."
PN-S10-10.D: "Pop any blisters that form so the burn can drain."

PN-S10-11.A: "I'll wear them only at night while I'm sleeping, and take them off in the morning."
PN-S10-11.C: "I'll wear them every day for 1 week, and then I can stop."
PN-S10-11.D: "They're only for comfort, so I can wear them when I feel like it."

PN-S10-12.A: Give the prescribed pain medication right after the dressing change is finished
PN-S10-12.C: Skip the dressing change today and let the client rest until the pain improves
PN-S10-12.D: Tell the client that the pain is unavoidable and that the change will be over quickly

PN-S10-14.A: "Apply it only to the itchy areas, such as between your fingers and on your wrists, then leave it on overnight and wash it off in the morning."
PN-S10-14.C: "Apply it from your neck down to your feet for just 10 minutes, then rinse it off completely in a warm shower before you go to bed."
PN-S10-14.D: "You don't need to wash your bedding or clothing after the treatment, since the cream will take care of the mites on your body."

PN-S10-16.A: "Give the child a long, hot bath every day to soften the skin and soothe the itching."
PN-S10-16.C: "Dress the child in soft wool clothing to keep the skin warm and protected."
PN-S10-16.D: "Use a gently scented soap and bubble bath to make bath time more relaxing."

PN-S10-17.A: "Keep your feet moist by applying lotion between your toes after you shower."
PN-S10-17.C: "It's fine to wear the same pair of socks for several days if they don't look dirty."
PN-S10-17.D: "Walking barefoot in the gym locker room and showers is fine for your feet."

PN-S10-19.A: "Take long, hot showers twice a day to keep your skin clean and comfortable."
PN-S10-19.C: "Use alcohol-based lotions on your skin after bathing to relieve the itch."
PN-S10-19.D: "Bathe with an antibacterial soap every day to prevent skin infections."

PN-S10-20.A: "Acne is normal for teenagers, so you really don't need to worry about it."
PN-S10-20.C: "Just ignore them, and they'll stop staring at you after a while."
PN-S10-20.D: "Your acne really isn't that bad. I'm sure no one else even notices."

PN-S10-21.A: Rub the fingers vigorously between the nurse's hands to warm them
PN-S10-21.C: Apply a heating pad set on high to the fingers to warm them quickly
PN-S10-21.D: Rub the fingers with snow to restore circulation gradually

PN-S10-22.A: An area of redness over the sacrum that blanches when pressed and fades within a few minutes
PN-S10-22.C: Dry, slightly flaky skin over the sacrum and lower back with no color change
PN-S10-22.D: Normal skin color with no change in temperature or firmness over the sacrum

PN-S10-23.A: Keep the affected leg in a dependent position below heart level
PN-S10-23.C: Apply a tight elastic bandage from the toes up to the knee each morning
PN-S10-23.D: Encourage the client to walk long distances several times a day

PN-S11-01.C: IV fluid infused over the shift

PN-S11-04.A: Offer the resident one large glass of water once per shift with medications
PN-S11-04.C: Restrict fluids after breakfast to reduce nighttime incontinence
PN-S11-04.D: Offer only caffeinated beverages such as coffee and cola

PN-S11-05.A: "Crush the tablets and mix them into applesauce if they're hard for you to swallow."
PN-S11-05.C: "Take them on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before breakfast."
PN-S11-05.D: "Chew each tablet well before you swallow it so it's absorbed faster."

PN-S11-06.B: A glass of low-fat milk with cereal at breakfast each morning
PN-S11-06.C: White rice served as a side dish with dinner each night
PN-S11-06.D: Apple juice diluted with water as an afternoon snack

PN-S11-07.B: White bread, plain pasta, rice crackers, and unfortified breakfast cereals
PN-S11-07.C: Skinless chicken breast with white rice, steamed green beans, and plain apple juice
PN-S11-07.D: Apples, grapes, watermelon, and other fresh fruits without added calcium

PN-S11-09.A: Continue the infusion at the same rate and recheck in 1 hour
PN-S11-09.C: Increase the IV rate to keep the client hydrated
PN-S11-09.D: Encourage the client to drink more oral fluids

PN-S11-10.A: Apply pressure to the site and continue the infusion at the same rate
PN-S11-10.C: Flush the line with saline to check whether the catheter is patent
PN-S11-10.D: Wrap the arm tightly with tape to secure the catheter in place

PN-S11-11.A: Cool, pale, and swollen skin all around the insertion site
PN-S11-11.C: Clear fluid leaking from under the dressing at the insertion site
PN-S11-11.D: Blanched, tight skin with no pain at the insertion site

PN-S11-15.A: A client with anxiety who is breathing rapidly and deeply during a panic attack today
PN-S11-15.C: A client who has had several days of watery diarrhea and poor oral intake
PN-S11-15.D: A client who takes calcium carbonate antacids several times a day for heartburn

PN-S11-16.A: Leave the client alone in a quiet, dim room to calm down
PN-S11-16.C: Encourage the client to breathe faster and more deeply to relax
PN-S11-16.D: Apply a nonrebreather mask with oxygen at 15 L/min

PN-S11-17.B: Hemoglobin A1C and fasting blood glucose every 3 months
PN-S11-17.C: Pupil size and reaction to light with each set of vital signs
PN-S11-17.D: Hearing acuity only, checked at each clinic visit

PN-S11-18.A: Full-strength apple juice offered in a sippy cup at meals
PN-S11-18.C: Carbonated soda that has been allowed to go flat
PN-S11-18.D: Plain water only, given in large amounts several times an hour

PN-S11-19.A: Bulging anterior fontanel when the infant is upright
PN-S11-19.C: Increased tears when the infant is crying
PN-S11-19.D: Weight gain since the last clinic visit

PN-S11-20.A: Encourage the resident to continue gardening in the shade
PN-S11-20.C: Cover the resident with a blanket to prevent chills
PN-S11-20.D: Give an antipyretic and wait 30 minutes to recheck

PN-S11-23.A: A plain bagel with cream cheese and a cup of black coffee
PN-S11-23.C: White toast with grape jelly and a cup of tea
PN-S11-23.D: Pancakes with maple syrup, whipped butter, and black coffee
